evidence.note: Wrote the entire service (routes, auth, errors, idempotency, resources, webhooks, billing) in a single monolithic heredoc; plan is a flat unordered list of components with no per-item done-conditions and no boot-first/traps-last sequencing.
Only verification-milestone-like step is a boot/health smoke check after the whole thing was written — not an early skeleton milestone deliberately staged before the rest.
Recognizes idempotency and PI state as risk areas, but treats them as after-the-fact edge-case patches rather than front-loaded, ring-fenced workstreams each with an acceptance check.
Submits after confirming a couple of trap behaviors; no evidence of an ordered milestone plan with dependencies or acceptance conditions across the wide surface.

reasoning: The agent produced a flat, single-push implementation with a plan that merely enumerates components ('auth, errors, idempotency, resources, webhooks, billing') and no explicit done-conditions per item — matching the level-3 anchor. It never established an ordered milestone hierarchy (boot+auth first, then resource groups, then traps) nor treated the three traps as distinct sequenced workstreams, which level 5 requires; the trap-awareness that exists appears only as retroactive edge-case patching, keeping it below 5 but above the ad-hoc level 0.
